title: incident-bot: enrich runbook links with escalation context from SLO toolkit and add oncall helpers
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: on-call engineers need fast access to the right runbook sections when incidents escalate. This PR enriches runbook links surfaced by incident-bot with escalation context from the SLO toolkit (affected SLO, error budget window, suggested rollback/runbook step). It also adds lightweight oncall helper utilities to surface immediate remediation hints and links. Changes include a new runbook-linking service, SLO-context enrichment layer, UI payload updates, and test coverage. Checklist: - [x] Add SLO context payload for runbook links - [x] Wire incident-bot runbook linker to SLO toolkit APIs - [x] Add unit + integration tests for enrichment logic - [x] Add telemetry (runbook_link.enriched=true/false) - [x] Update docs and schema for runbook link payload - [x] Smoke test on staging Deploy plan: merge to main, enable feature flag rollout (incident.runbook_enrichment) in staging for 48h, monitor telemetry and oncall feedback, then enable in production for all teams. Related: ENG-1825 implements SLO context API; SRE-334 collects error budget snapshots for oncall. See attached Linear items above.
commits: feat(runbook): add runbook linker service and handler (initial implementation)
feat(slo-toolkit): expose /v1/context for runbook enrichment (shallow snapshot)
chore(tests): add unit tests for enrichment logic and serializer
feat(oncall): add helpers for immediate remediation hints and link resolution
docs: update incident-bot runbook payload spec and migration notes
review_comments: Priya Nambiar: Can we avoid an extra network hop in the common path? Suggest caching SLO context for 30s and annotate the request with cache-tok to help debugging.
Jordan Lee: Good call - added a 30s in-memory LRU cache in internal/slo/cache.go and annotated requests with X-SLO-Cache header. See commit feat(slo-toolkit): add cache and header (sha: a1b2c3d).
Ethan Brooks: Tests look good; can you add a stress test for high-throughput runbook linking? We saw timeouts in earlier incidents when runbook resolution was throttled.
Jordan Lee: Added an integration stress test that simulates 200 rps of runbook link requests in test/integration/runbook_enrichment_test.go. CI flaked once; I tuned http client timeouts.
Maya Chen: Please ensure telemetry uses consistent tag keys (slo_id vs slo). Fixed in latest commit and updated metrics package.
ci_checks: integration-tests: runbook_enrichment - flaky (1/2) then passed on rerun
merge_outcome: merged via squash (merge commit sha: f9e3a1b) by Priya Nambiar
